key_insight: Parallel cell iteration with on-die retention BIST is the right test method; fold it into each dossier's test plan rather than treating it as an invention.
killer_doubt: Logic MPWs lack the IGZO, high-k MIM and HAR modules where the open unknowns live; 200 variants on ~10 mm2 give ~1e4 cells each, blind to 1e-6 retention tails.
decisive_experiment: One GF180 shuttle: 20 variants x 64 kb with BIST plus a 1 Mb reference array; check whether lognormal fits from 1e4 cells predict the measured 1e-5 tail. ~$40k.
prior_art: Gain-cell eDRAM MPW test chips (Bar-Ilan, EPFL groups); foundry retention test vehicles; open-PDK shuttle supply fragile since Efabless closed in 2025.

key_insight: Measuring k, leakage and breakdown on one wafer at final thickness is the right screen; libraries cheaply map the k-versus-band-gap frontier.
killer_doubt: k and band gap trade off (Eg near ~3 eV at k 70-100); 50-100 nm sputtered films overstate k versus 5-8 nm ALD in 60:1 holes with interfacial dead layers.
decisive_experiment: Run the library at 6 nm on TiN/Ru with a 450 C anneal; go only if any spot shows EOT <=0.4 nm at <=1e-7 A/cm2 and 0.8 V. ~$150k.
prior_art: Van Dover et al. Bell Labs Zr-Sn-Ti-O composition spread (Nature 1998); Intermolecular combinatorial high-k programme with Elpida for DRAM (~2010).

key_insight: Computation can prune ternary oxide space before costly ALD; a >=4 eV band-gap filter is the right gate for DRAM leakage.
killer_doubt: A ~1,800-oxide HSE screen already exists; its standout (rocksalt BeO) is a metastable high-pressure phase. Even k 70 cuts AR only 75 to ~45, 1.6x.
decisive_experiment: Refilter the published 1,800-oxide dataset for cations with mature ALD precursors; grow the top three at 6 nm and 400 C; go if EOT <=0.35 nm at <=1e-7 A/cm2. ~$200k.
prior_art: Yim, Han, Hwang et al., NPG Asia Materials 2015: ~1,800 oxides screened for k and band gap (via search snippet); Materials Project DFPT dielectric data.

key_insight: Temperature is a real leakage knob: SRH generation (Ea ~0.56 eV) falls ~1e9 from 300 to 150 K; commercial DDR3 at 77 K retains 4,096 s.
killer_doubt: Grain-boundary trap-assisted tunnelling and GIDL (Ea <=0.15 eV) fall only ~30-300x at 150 K; warm IGZO already reaches aA/um; cooling costs ~2.5-4 W per W.
decisive_experiment: Measure Ioff from 300 K to 120 K at hold bias on 1,000 small-gate SPC/LTPS poly-Si TFTs; compare the 1e-4 leakage tail with IGZO at 300 K. ~$100k.
prior_art: Cryogenic DRAM work (Rambus/Microsoft 2017, CryoRAM, CryoGuard); our B5-14 77 K oxide stage; Kioxia OCTRAM and IGZO 2T0C win without cooling.

key_insight: Accelerators carry tens of uF of on-die and interposer capacitance; seeing it as idle charge storage is clever framing.
killer_doubt: A cap holding data cannot decouple: droops arrive in ns, evicting 150 MB takes ms. 50 fF cells plus a transistor each give only SRAM-class density.
decisive_experiment: GPU power-trace study: fraction of time half the decap can be removed with droop under 20 mV, versus scratch demand at those moments; drop if anti-correlated. ~$50k.
prior_art: IBM deep-trench eDRAM and trench decaps share one module (POWER7-9); Intel Crystalwell MIM eDRAM; TSMC eDTC capacitors in CoWoS interposers.

key_insight: Bond-free ion displacement inside a cage avoids the charge-fluence wear that kills tunnel-write cells, so endurance could genuinely be unlimited.
killer_doubt: Flipping a 0.8 eV well over ~0.2 nm in ns needs ~4 V/nm local field, cage-screened further, above ~1 V/nm breakdown; one dipole moves a 100 nm2 FET ~10 mV.
decisive_experiment: STM on a Li+@C60 or Sc3N@C80 monolayer at 300 K: measure dipole-flip barrier from telegraph lifetimes and the tip switching field; kill if barrier <0.5 eV or field >1 V/nm. ~$150k.
prior_art: Li+@C60 isolated and structurally characterised (Aoyagi et al., Nature Chem 2010); ZettaCore molecular memory; no endohedral-dipole memory array found.

key_insight: Capacitor height becomes slice thickness, decoupling aspect ratio from plasma etch; hollow drawn nanochannel glass already reached ~33 nm channels, a workable template variant.
killer_doubt: Liquid-metal cores below ~100 nm break up by Rayleigh-Plateau in ~ms during the draw; a multi-fibre lattice cannot register to a 40 nm-pitch transistor array after bonding.
decisive_experiment: Draw a hollow nanochannel-glass slice (50 nm pores, 5 um thick), ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN, bond to an oversized-pad array; measure Cs spread and opens/shorts over 1e6 pads. ~$400k.
prior_art: NRL nanochannel glass, 33 nm channels (Tonucci et al., Science 1992); multimaterial fibre drawing (MIT, Bilkent); our N-21 AAO-Cap grows a registered mold in place.

key_insight: IGZO gain-cell retention (1e3-3e4 s) matches long-context session spans; droop as soft eviction plus zero-detect reclaim fits decay-gated models with zero refresh.
killer_doubt: Cell retention spreads >=2 decades and halves per ~10 C, so decay is uncontrolled noise, not ALiBi; refresh for 43 GB of KV costs only ~0.25 W.
decisive_experiment: Software: inject lognormal retention spread (sigma 0.5-1 decade) and 2x per 10 C drift into KV caches of an open 8B model; go if long-context loss <1% versus 2-bit KV. ~$30k.
prior_art: RANA retention-aware training (ISCA 2018); StreamingLLM and H2O eviction; RetNet and Mamba decay gates; our B4-06 graceful-forgetting KV holds the core.

key_insight: Capacitive crosspoint coding avoids DC sneak paths, so a transistor-free multi-layer ROM in standard BEOL is sound in principle for frozen weights.
killer_doubt: A via stub adds ~4 aF to an ~8 fF, 512-cell sense line: ~0.5 mV. At 40 nm, ~120 nm metal pitch makes 8 planes ~2,000 nm2/bit, worse than DRAM.
decisive_experiment: Field-solve stub coupling on a 40 nm stack, then tape out a 4 kb array on an MPW (~$80k); kill if signal <10 mV at 64 cells per sense line.
prior_art: IBM card capacitor read-only storage on System/360 (1960s); Apollo core rope; via and contact mask ROM; hardwired-model chips (Taalas).

key_insight: Frozen weights need neither refresh nor endurance, so a write-once store can legitimately offload them from HBM: a real demand-side lever.
killer_doubt: Mature-node ROM at ~0.03 um2/bit costs ~$10-20/GB to make, 7-14x DRAM's $1.48; selector-free 1-2F2 crosspoints have sneak paths; models churn every 3-6 months.
decisive_experiment: Cost model plus one shuttle: a 28 nm via-ROM macro with 2-level via resistance; measure density, read energy and level margin over 1e6 bits; compare cost per GB with HBF NAND. ~$150k.
prior_art: Via and contact mask ROM (decades); Taalas hardwired-model inference chips; SanDisk/SK hynix High Bandwidth Flash serves read-mostly weights and stays updatable.

key_insight: A steep nonlinear element on the storage node to cut needed charge is the right goal; triage confirms reading few-hundred-electron nodes is solvable.
killer_doubt: 300 e under 100 nm2 is 3e14 cm-2: at EOT 1 nm the node must sit at ~14 V. Electrostatic gates reach ~3e13 cm-2; NdNiO3 is metallic at 300 K.
decisive_experiment: Gate a 3 nm SmNiO3 film (TMI ~400 K) through 3 nm HfO2 at room temperature; kill if resistance changes <3x at 1.5 V, versus a Si MOSFET's 100x per 120 mV. ~$100k.
prior_art: Field-effect gating of NdNiO3 (Scherwitzl et al. 2010) and ionic-liquid nickelate gating; Mott-FET proposals (IBM, 1998); oxide 2T0C gain cells already give in-cell gain.

key_insight: A thick-oxide write device with negative hold bias reaches ~10 aA, giving ~1-10 s retention in U.S.-fabbed open PDKs: useful for chiplet test vehicles.
killer_doubt: A 3T thick-oxide cell is ~3-5 um2/bit (~0.25 Mb/mm2), about 1,500x below 1-beta DRAM; junction leakage rises ~100x at 85 C, cutting retention to ~0.1 s.
decisive_experiment: One GF180 or SKY130 shuttle: 64 kb 3T arrays, retention distribution at 25 and 85 C; a weeks-scale result, not a moonshot. ~$20k.
prior_art: Intel 1103 three-transistor DRAM (1970); Bar-Ilan and EPFL long-retention gain-cell eDRAM in 180-65 nm; open-PDK gain-cell projects on SKY130.
